summary: Ephemeral auth cookie fragmentation triggers truncated idempotency token, causing duplicate function/tool executions on retry
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicated external webhook/tool invocations when their app sends long-running function calls through Redwood hosted API. The duplication happens intermittently after client retries. Impact: repeated downstream work and billing surprises for the customer. Hypothesis: idempotency token getting truncated or re-encoded by our edge proxy when transmitted as part of a session cookie leading retries to be treated as new requests.
impact: Customer observed 2–3 duplicated webhook/tool invocations for 8% of long-running funcall requests during peak, causing ~USD 1.2k of extra downstream work over 24 hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer SDK (Python and TS) initiates a streaming function call with an idempotency token set in client metadata. In this integration the token is attached both as X-Idempotency-Key header and mirrored into a session cookie by an intermediary service.
2) Network path: client -> CDN edge (customer-managed) -> Redwood edge-proxy -> Redwood API -> serving-runtime.

3) Simulate intermittent latency by delaying the upstream ack (long-running function, >5s). Client-side SDK triggers retry logic (after 4s timeout) and reconnects using same idempotency token but cookie value now appears truncated at the edge.
4) Observe two tool/webhook calls on the customer's downstream service for the same logical operation.
5) Reproduction is flaky; requires specific cookie length (~>900 bytes) and chunking behavior at the customer CDN.
observed_behavior: Retries are accepted as new requests (no dedupe). Downstream tooling receives duplicate HTTP POSTs with different idempotency token values (truncated vs full). SDKs show success for both attempts.
expected_behavior: Retries with the same logical idempotency key should be de-duplicated by Redwood runtime regardless of intermediary cookie rewrites. Idempotency canonicalization should prefer X-Idempotency-Key header over cookies and normalize encoding.
logs: edge-proxy (2026-03-12T14:03:21Z) INFO incoming request: client_ip=52.12.34.56 path=/v1/functions/execute headers={Cookie: session=eyJpZGVudGl0eS1rZXkiOiAiYWJj...<truncated>}
edge-proxy (2026-03-12T14:03:25Z) WARN cookie-length-exceeded: len=1026 limit=1024; trimming applied
serving-runtime (2026-03-12T14:03:25Z) INFO funcall-start id=fn-abc123 idempotency_key=abcde12345fgh (note: header X-Idempotency-Key present)
serving-runtime (2026-03-12T14:03:30Z) INFO funcall-start id=fn-abc124 idempotency_key=abcde123 (truncated in cookie representation)
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: customer trace shows two separate requests reaching our runtime with differing idempotency token values despite client sending the same token header.

Edge SRE found edge-proxy config that rewrites cookies for session stitching and enforces a 1024 byte cookie header limit; when the cookie value exceeds the threshold the proxy performs a truncate operation without promoting the canonical X-Idempotency-Key header.

Customer-confirmed: their upstream CDN mirrors metadata into a large session cookie (contains additional JWTs and metadata), which is sometimes chunked into multiple Set-Cookie headers; our edge-proxy concatenation logic then performs a silent trim.

SDK behavior: Python SDK gracefully sends X-Idempotency-Key header. TS SDK (older pinned version) relied on cookie propagation for idempotency in their custom integration and did not retry with header fallback.

Hypothesis: when the edge truncates the cookie it leaves the X-Idempotency-Key header intact for some requests but not for others because of upstream connection reuse; in the truncated cases our request normalization code prefers cookie-derived idempotency and overwrites header value with cookie-derived normalized token, resulting in mismatch and therefore duplicate processing.
Repro script: provided a curl + header + cookie replication and able to reproduce 2/10 attempts locally when cookie size crosses 1024 bytes and CDN introduces chunking.
Risk assessment: High for integrations that mirror idempotency to cookies or that embed long metadata in cookies. Low for customers following header-only idempotency best practices.
Related issues: SUP-824000 (edge-proxy cookie-limit behavior) — linked for edge config context.
comments: Priya Nair (Support): Customer reported 2x duplicate webhooks for function calls originating from their TS client. Attached initial logs. Asking SRE for edge-config review.
Marcus Lee (Oncall SRE): Confirmed cookie trim at edge-proxy. Working on a canary config to prioritize header idempotency canonicalization. Will coordinate SDK team for backwards-compatibility patch.

Elena Ruiz (Eng - SDK): We'll ship a TS SDK patch that ensures client will always send X-Idempotency-Key header and will not rely on cookies. Also add a defensive header-only dedupe rule on the runtime.
Customer (FathomAI - A. Chen): Can you confirm hotfix ETA? We're seeing duplicates every 10–15 minutes during peak traffic windows. This is impacting customer invoices.
Marcus Lee: Target hotfix for edge-proxy config rollout at 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC to prefer X-Idempotency-Key and log any cookie-derived overrides for 48h. SDK patch scheduled for 2026-03-14.
Priya Nair: Added mitigation steps for customer — temporary workaround to remove idempotency mirror from their CDN or reduce cookie size below 900 bytes.
resolution: Partial fix applied: edge-proxy config updated to canonicalize idempotency from X-Idempotency-Key header and ignore cookie-derived tokens when header present. Canary rolled out to 10% of edges on 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC. TS and Python SDK guidance updated; TS SDK patch v1.4.3 published to explicitly set X-Idempotency-Key and avoid cookie mirroring. Customer applied temporary workaround.
resolution_notes: Canary metrics show duplicate toolcall rate dropped from 8% -> 0.3% on canary edges. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC after 24h canary validation. Follow-up: add linting rule in Console to warn when customers mirror idempotency into cookies and update docs.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Complete full rollout of edge change and monitor duplicate rates for 72h.
2) Release TS SDK patch to all channels, notify customers via release notes.
3) Create a Console lint/warning for cookie-mirrored idempotency usage.
4) Postmortem note and customer-facing RCA to be published after full rollout.
